w: The sullen skepticism of your eyes For ever trying to transcend itself, Is often entered by a wistful elf Who sits naïvely unperturbed and wise.
Rows of blankly box-like buildings Raise their sodden architecture Into the poised lyric of the sky.
O unresisting street-pavement, Keep your passive insolence At the dwarfs who scorn you with their feet.
Yet, on a Sunday afternoon I have seen you straightening your backs with slow smiles; Walking through the streets And patiently groping for lost outlines.
August sauntered down the mountain-side, Dropping mottled, turbid wraiths of decay.
A man stood at one window, His gaunt face trembling underneath A feverish jauntiness.
Beneath your heaving flash of limbs Your thoughts are smashed to a dejected trance And you are swept, like empty mites, Into a glistening frenzy of motion....
Undistinguished butter-cup Lost among myriads of others, To the red ant eyeing you You are giant stillness.
The steel-mill chimneys fling their gaunt seeking A little distance into the red That softly combs their smoky hair.
From that day on the snake was filled With little, meek whispers of concern.
Yet, on a Sunday afternoon I have seen you straightening your backs with slow smiles; Walking through the streets And patiently groping for lost outlines.
Crisp inanities ripple back and forth Among these three, like ghostly parrots Visiting each other’s cages.
Her numbly waxen, cherub face Emerges gently from the doorway’s blackness As though the dark had given birth to it.
Through the turbulent servility Of a churlish city street He strides opaquely; nothing in his walk Resembles an advancing gleam.
The cool and indiscriminate glare Of sunlight seems to desecrate a tomb, And the racing people seem A stream of accidental shadows.
Upon this nervous shop-girl’s face, Where clusters of tiny limpness meet, A frightened spark leaps high and drops Into the hot pause of a banished love.
Knights and kings flooded my song, Catching with their glittering clash The unheard boldness in my life.
This woman’s face is scorched By a torch that falls from weary hands And makes her laugh an unheard lie.
Perhaps upon your death-beds You will lift your hands, with a wraith of grace, Showing life a last, weak curve Of the rhythm he could not kill.
But, looking down, he spied A softly wild cheeked mountain pool, And there a handful of fairy nuts Bit into the indigo cupping them.
His eyes were hungrily upturned To where the stars hung--icily clustered nuts Dotting trees of solitude.
Endless feet tap over you With a maniac insistence.
Three crows in a row Search for clearer tongues, with steady discords.
People laugh when I say that my doll is alive, But if she were dead, my fingers Wouldn’t know that they were touching her.
RATTLE-SNAKE MOUNTAIN And thus evening bows into morning.
A trolley-car speeds by And seems a strident lyric of motion.
The colours in my room Meet each other and hesitate.
The morning hides from their eyes: They walk on, in great strides, Like blind men swinging over a well-known scene.
And then the falling light reveals That something of a village hangs about her: Something slumbering and ample.
With a languid impudence I have tarried underneath the moon, While the haggard reticence Of their lives forgot itself within me!
